title: Tortellini Alfredo
author: Marco Bellini
desc: Tortellini Alfredo takes Bologna's classic filled pasta out of its traditional broth and tosses it instead in a rich, silky butter-and-Parmigiano sauce, for a more indulgent alternative presentation.
longDesc: While purists in Emilia-Romagna serve tortellini exclusively in brodo, tossing them in a buttery Parmigiano sauce has become a widely loved alternative, especially outside the region, letting the delicate meat filling shine against a rich, creamy backdrop.
ingredients: 1 batch fresh tortellini (as in ITA034, using the same filling and shaping method)
100 g (1¼ cups) finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano, plus more for serving
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil and cook the tortellini for 3–4 minutes until they float and the pasta is tender.
Reserve at least 1 cup of pasta water before draining.
In a large skillet, melt the butter over low heat.
Add the drained tortellini directly to the skillet along with a splash of pasta water, tossing gently to coat without breaking the delicate pasta.
Off the heat, gradually add the Parmigiano, tossing continuously and adding pasta water as needed to build a smooth, glossy sauce.
Serve immediately, garnished with parsley and extra Parmigiano.
chefTips: Toss gently rather than vigorously to avoid breaking the delicate, filled pasta.
Room-temperature butter emulsifies more smoothly than cold butter.
Fresh tortellini gives the best result, but good-quality store-bought works well too if short on time.
commonMistakes: Tossing too roughly, causing the tortellini to split open and lose their filling.
Overcooking the tortellini, making the delicate pasta wrapper mushy.
Adding the cheese over too much heat, causing the sauce to break rather than emulsify.
storage: Best eaten immediately — the sauce does not hold or reheat well.
reheating: Not recommended; make fresh for the best texture.
healthBenefits: A good source of protein from the meat-filled pasta.
A good source of calcium from the Parmigiano.
culturalNote: While tortellini in brodo remains the most traditional preparation in Bologna, tossing tortellini in butter and cheese has become a beloved variation enjoyed throughout Italy and internationally.
